name: Index Packaging, Inc.
old_description: Index Packaging’s manufacturing facility in Milton, New Hampshire specializes in wood packaging products, including wood crates and wood pallets, both new and recycled. Since we control the entire production process and have our own fleet of vehicles serving New England, we can guarantee your order will be on time.
about:
Index Packaging, Inc. was founded in 1968 by Bill and Connie Lander in the basement of their New York home. The company moved to Milton, New Hampshire in 1981 and remains a closely held, family‑owned corporation now led by second‑generation shareholders including Bruce Lander, Debora Lussier, and Connie Lander. From its start as a small packaging operation, it has grown into a midsize manufacturer with four production and warehouse campuses across New Hampshire.

The company designs and manufactures custom packaging for fragile or high‑value items, producing foam inserts, corrugated boxes, wood crates and pallets, and specialty shippers such as apple gift boxes. All three material streams—foam, wood, and corrugated—are processed under one roof across facilities totaling more than 275,000 square feet. In‑house capabilities include design and engineering, prototyping, CNC foam fabrication, corrugated converting, wood crate assembly, kiln‑drying to ISPM‑15 standards, vendor‑managed inventory, warehousing, and a dedicated trucking fleet for New England delivery plus nationwide LTL and parcel shipping. The operation employs over 200 people.

Index Packaging serves industrial equipment manufacturers, military and defense contractors, medical and pharmaceutical companies, laboratories, and food and agriculture businesses. Concrete examples include custom crates for sensitive instrumentation, foam‑filled shippers for fruit and produce, and protective packaging for cell‑phone and electronics shipments.

The business was built on a “Protection by Design” philosophy that emphasizes service, quality, and quick decision‑making enabled by its family ownership. An internal recycling program diverts polyurethane and polyethylene foam, corrugated scrap, and wood waste into secondary markets, and the company’s own logistics network allows it to guarantee on‑time delivery throughout New England.
